info.title: Apps Observability API
info.description:
The Apps Observability API allows VTEX account integrators and developers to query logs and metrics from [VTEX IO apps](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/guides/vtex-io-documentation-what-is-a-vtex-app) in a Grafana-compatible format. Use it to build dashboards, run ad-hoc queries, and list available fields and apps.

## Endpoint requirements

All endpoints under `/api/extensions/observability` require authentication via API key (X-VTEX-API-AppKey and X-VTEX-API-AppToken). The cache configuration endpoints are restricted to internal network access only.

## Index

### Logs

- ``POST`` [Query logs](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/api-reference/observability-api#post-/api/extensions/observability/logs/-tenant-/query)
- ``GET`` [Get logs fields](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/api-reference/observability-api#get-/api/extensions/observability/logs/-tenant-/fields)

### Metrics

- ``POST`` [Query metrics](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/api-reference/observability-api#post-/api/extensions/observability/metrics/-tenant-/query)
- ``GET`` [Get metrics fields](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/api-reference/observability-api#get-/api/extensions/observability/metrics/-tenant-/fields)
- ``GET`` [Get metric names](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/api-reference/observability-api#get-/api/extensions/observability/metrics/-tenant-/-app-/names)

### Apps

- ``GET`` [Get apps](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/api-reference/observability-api#get-/api/extensions/observability/-tenant-/apps)

### Capabilities

- ``GET`` [Get capabilities](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/api-reference/observability-api#get-/api/extensions/observability/capabilities)

post.description:
Executes a logs query for the given tenant with filters, pagination, and optional aggregations. Returns data in [Grafana DataFrame format](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/developers/plugins/data-frames/).

## Rate Limits & Quotas

The API enforces rate limits and quotas per tenant:

| Resource | Limit |
| :---- | :---- |
| Query timeout | 30 seconds |
| Maximum page size | 1000 rows |
| Default page size | 50 rows |

> ℹ️ Contact VTEX support if you need higher limits for your account.

## Best Practices

### Query performance

1. **Always filter by time**: Include `TimestampTime` filters to limit data scanned.
2. **Use specific filters**: Filter by `app` when possible.
3. **Limit columns**: Request only the columns you need.
4. **Use pagination**: Fetch data in smaller pages for large result sets.

### Time range recommendations

| Query Type | Recommended Range |
| :---- | :---- |
| Real-time monitoring | Last 5-15 minutes |
| Hourly analysis | Last 1-6 hours |
| Daily reports | Last 24 hours |
| Historical analysis | Up to retention limit |

## Permissions

Any user or [API key](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/guides/api-authentication-using-api-keys) must have at least one of the appropriate [License Manager resources](https://help.vtex.com/en/tutorial/license-manager-resources--3q6ztrC8YynQf6rdc6euk3) to be able to successfully run this request. Otherwise, they will receive a status code `403` error. These are the applicable resources for this endpoint:

| **Product** | **Category** | **Resource** |
| --- | ----- | ----- |
| VTEX IO | Infrastructure | **Log Access - Read-only** |

There are no applicable [predefined roles](https://help.vtex.com/en/tutorial/predefined-roles--jGDurZKJHvHJS13LnO7Dy) for this resource list. You must [create a custom role](https://help.vtex.com/en/tutorial/roles--7HKK5Uau2H6wxE1rH5oRbc#creating-a-role) and add at least one of the resources above in order to use this endpoint.

To learn more about machine authentication at VTEX, see [Authentication overview](https://developers.vtex.com/docs/guides/authentication-overview#machine-authentication).

Executes a metrics query for the given tenant with filters, pagination, and optional aggregations. Returns data in [Grafana DataFrame format](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/developers/plugins/data-frames/).

## Metric Types

The platform supports three metric types from OpenTelemetry:

| Type | Description | Use Cases | Aggregation |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `gauge` | Point-in-time value | CPU usage, memory, temperature | `avg`, `min`, `max` |
| `sum` | Cumulative counter | Request count, bytes transferred | `sum` |
| `histogram` | Distribution of values | Response time, request size | `sum`, `count` |

### Metric Type Detection

The API automatically stores and handles different metric types. Filter by `MetricType` to query specific types:

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "column": "MetricType",
      "operator": "=",
      "type": "string",
      "value": "histogram"
    }
  ]
}
```

4. **Use pagination**: Fetch data in smaller pages for large result sets.

FilterOperator.title: operator
FilterOperator.description:
Filter operator. The table below shows the available operators:

| Operator | Alias | Description | Example Value |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| `=` | `eq` | Equal to | `"value"` |
| `>` | `gt` | Greater than | `100` |
| `<` | `lt` | Less than | `100` |
| `>=` | `gte` | Greater than or equal | `100` |
| `<=` | `lte` | Less than or equal | `100` |
| `!=` | `ne` | Not equal | `"value"` |
| `LIKE` | `like` | Contains pattern | `"search"` |
| `NOT LIKE` | `not_like` | Does not contain | `"exclude"` |
| `IN` | `in` | In list | `["a", "b", "c"]` |
| `NOT IN` | `not_in` | Not in list | `["x", "y"]` |
| `BETWEEN` | `between` | Between two values | `[100, 200]` |
| `IS NULL` | `is_null` | Value is null | N/A |
| `IS NOT NULL` | `is_not_null` | Value is not null | N/A |
